newsitem.title: USA: Ford says exploring idea of Budget sale.
newsitem.headline: Ford says exploring idea of Budget sale.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said it is exploring the idea of a sale of Budget Rent a Car Corp, which it is in the process of buying.
Ford spokesman Chris Vinyard said Wednesday the automaker does not plan to make any announcements regarding Budget following Ford's regularly scheduled board of directors meeting Thursday.
"We're looking at the idea that a sale could be done," Vinyard said of Budget.

Ford last year announced that it would acquire all of the common stock in privately held Budget for an undisclosed price. At the same time, Ford took a $437-million after-tax charge against its second-quarter 1996 earnings to write down the value of loans to Budget and Ford's preferred stock in the rental car agency.
Ford also owns the largest U.S. auto rental agency, Park Ridge, N.J.-based Hertz Corp. Ford's purchase of Budget has been delayed by a U.S. Federal Trade Commission anti-trust review.
Vinyard declined to say whether Ford would complete the purchase of Budget shares before a possible sale to a third party.

Lisle, Ill.-based Budget has been closely allied with Ford for many years and rents mainly Ford vehicles. Ford's purchase of the rental car company was aimed at improving the performance of the automaker's investment in Budget, then ranked as the fourth-largest U.S. car rental car company.

Vinyard declined to comment specifically on an article in Wednesday's Wall Street Journal that said Ford was expected to sell Budget to Team Rental Group Inc, a Daytona, Fla.-based Budget licensee, for about $350 million.
However, Vinyard said Ford has begun to explore the possibility of a sale of Budget because of recently rising investor interest in the rental car industry.
"Interest in the group in the last six to 10 months has increased significantly," Vinyard said.
Three of the top five rental car firms have changed hands in the past four months.
Avis Inc, the second-largest U.S. agency, was recently acquired by HFS Inc for about $800 million.

Republic Industries Inc, headed by noted investor Wayne Huizenga, recently agreed to buy National Car Rental System Inc for about $600 million from a private investor group. Republic acquired Alamo Rent a Car late last year.

Vinyard declined to say whether Ford was exploring a possible sale of Hertz, but noted that Hertz has reported record-setting profits for three consecutive years. "We think they'll have another record this year," Vinyard said.
